title: Saul and the Witch of Endor
paragraphs: Saul and the Witch of Endor
Saul stood in the dark with a crown on his head and terror in his bones.
The Philistines were coming.
And God was silent.
“When Saul inquired of the LORD, the LORD did not answer him, either by dreams, or by Urim, or by prophets.” — 1 Samuel 28:6
Read that again.
A man can wear the crown and still lose the presence.

Saul knew the law.
Saul knew witchcraft was forbidden.
Saul had once removed mediums from the land.
But fear has a way of making hypocrites run back to what they once condemned.
So Saul disguised himself.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
He wasn’t just hiding from people.
He was trying to hide from God.
God saw it.
You knew.
In the night, Saul went to Endor and asked a medium to summon Samuel.
The same Saul who refused obedience now wanted spiritual answers.
But delayed desperation is not repentance.
“To obey is better than sacrifice.” — 1 Samuel 15:22
Samuel’s message was not comfort.
It was judgment.
“Because you did not obey the voice of the LORD… the LORD will give Israel also with you into the hand of the Philistines.” — 1 Samuel 28:18–19
Saul fell to the ground.
Not because he was holy.
Because he was exposed.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
This is the terrifying diagnosis:

Saul wanted guidance without surrender.
He wanted relief without repentance.
He wanted God’s voice while rejecting God’s authority.
And many people today are doing the same thing.

You want peace, but not obedience.
You want blessing, but not repentance.
You want Jesus as Savior, but not Lord.
God saw it.
But Saul’s story points us to the better King.

Saul failed.
Jesus obeyed.

Saul trembled before judgment.
Jesus bore judgment on the cross.
“Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners.” — 1 Timothy 1:15
The answer is not spiritual curiosity.
The answer is repentance and faith in Jesus Christ.

Turn from sin.
Run to Christ.
Grace is still open.
